note: Declarative approval policy, consumed by supervisor.mjs through the PermissionRequest hook and by wrapper-policy.mjs for wrapper-backed workers. 'allow' and 'deny' answer the worker directly; 'escalate' defers to canUseTool, which parks the request for the manager. Set SUPERVISOR_PERMISSION_LOG=<path> to append every request as JSONL — the escalated ones are what to promote into rules here.
note_bash: A Bash entry with "matchType": "command" is an ANCHORED whole-token prefix: `ls` covers `ls -la /tmp` but not `lsblk`, and the tokens AFTER the prefix are unconstrained — so a prefix is listed only when EVERY extension of it is read-only. That is why `sed` and `find` are absent (`sed -n -i`, `find -delete`), why no `git` prefix is listed at all (git runs commands named in the repo's own config; core.fsmonitor fires on `git status`), and why `sort` (`-o`, `--output`, `--compress-program`), `tree` (`-o`), `rg` (`--pre`), `file` (`-C`/`--compile` writes `<name>.mgc`), `diff` (`-l`/`--paginate` runs `pr(1)`) and `uniq` (its second positional is an OUTPUT file) are absent — a prefix rule cannot exclude a flag, so the only honest fix is not to list the command. server/manager-allowlist.test.mjs pins the same rule for the manager allowlist; this file must agree with it. A chained command is split on && || ; | by policy.mjs and allowed only when EVERY segment is allowed on its own, which is what makes `cd` safe to list: `cd /tmp && rm -rf /` still reaches the deny rule. Before this change the file carried NO Bash allow rule, so every Bash command — `ls -la /tmp` included — escalated to the operator.
